title: Three ways to perform the Hajj
note: The page's three parallel tracks of tamattu', qiran and ifrad, marking where ihram opens, closes, and where a sacrifice falls.

lines.text: Hajj has three shapes; you pick one first
At the miqat, for a Hajj in Dhul Hijjah
Tamattu: Umrah first, then out, then Hajj
Qiran: one ihram holds both, start to end
lines.sub: a sacrifice is due, as it is for tamattu

lines.text: Ifrad: Hajj alone, and no sacrifice falls
For qiran, most say one tawaf serves both
lines.sub: Hanafis require two tawafs, two sa'is

lines.text: Maliki and Shafi'i say ifrad is best
lines.sub: Hanafi picks qiran; Hanbali picks tamattu

lines.text: Whichever you pick, choose it before ihram

lines.eyebrow: The three ways, at the miqat
lines.src: The three ways to perform Hajj

research.retell: There are three ways to perform Hajj, tamattu, qiran and ifrad, chosen before entering ihram, and they differ in whether a sacrifice is owed and how the schools rank them.
proof: There is not one Hajj, there are three shapes of it, and you choose your shape before you enter ihram, not after.; The choice decides whether you owe a sacrifice, whether you get out of ihram in the middle, and how many times you perform tawaf and sa’i.
Nearly every group from outside Arabia performs the first one.; 8 Dhul Hijjah
Tamattu’, Umrah, out, then Hajj; You enter ihram for Umrah at the miqat, perform the Umrah, cut your hair, and come completely out of ihram... Then on the eighth of Dhul Hijjah you enter ihram again
Qiran, both in one ihram; You stay in the two cloths from the miqat until the tenth of Dhul Hijjah. A sacrifice is due, as it is for tamattu’.
Ifrad, Hajj alone; no hady due; no sacrifice is due from you, because you have not joined an Umrah to it; the only one of the three with no hady, no sacrifice, attached to it
Most schools hold that one tawaf and one sa’i serve for both the Umrah and the Hajj of the qarin. The Hanafis hold that he performs two tawafs and two sa’is, one set for each.
This is a famous four way disagreement, and every school has an argument that is not silly.; Hanafi: Qiran is best, because it joins two rites in one journey; Hanbali: Tamattu’ is best
Whichever you choose, choose it before you enter ihram, and tell your group leader, because the sacrifice, the timing of your hair cutting, and whether you repeat the sa’i all follow from it.
